scope: Current GateGoldJira implementation; future feature recommendations excluded.
testReferences: Related files only. No scenario/assertion coverage or current passing result is inferred.

areas.title: Authentication, sessions and company accounts
areas.summary: Atomic current account journeys, local-only password boundaries and managed identity candidates. Source-backed implementation status is not a runtime verification result. Existing test paths are related references, not claims of complete per-case coverage.

areas.title: Company and issue activity history
areas.summary: Attributed retained history, scoped access, date/resource filters and non-executing change display. Issue detail can consume the same history service. Related tests are references only.

areas.title: Unified attachments, private previews and recoverable uploads
areas.summary: Native queue and panel actions plus typed transfer boundaries. Distinguishes policy-driven file capacity, ten-MiB image/direct uploads and one-MiB chunks.

areas.title: Backlog planning, ranking and activation
areas.summary: Planned work has ordering independent of active board columns. Browser bulk activation processes at most 100 selected issues through individual organization commands; it is not one atomic bulk transaction.

areas.title: Boards, columns, card movement and filters
areas.summary: Current independent Kanban boards. Workflow/stage definitions belong to workflows; this area owns column mapping, board-local ranks and WIP. Existing test references are evidence locations, not fresh pass claims.

areas.title: Rich descriptions, discussion and selected mentions
areas.summary: Editor actions are documented independently for descriptions and comments because their capabilities differ. Notifications have their own area.

areas.title: Compatibility clients and retained data
areas.summary: Published V1 issue/board/media operations remain a distinct API/MCP surface. Current native web routes use V2 where available; compatibility projection is not permission to rewrite custom identities.

areas.title: Project taxonomy, typed custom fields and safe activation
areas.summary: Workflow/stage/transition/binding/migration and review-policy setup are canonical in workflows; this area retains taxonomy, defaults, custom-field lifecycle and activation guards. Existing test references do not certify execution or per-case coverage.

areas.title: Issue custom values, approval execution and reusable labels
areas.summary: Value behaviors separate from definition settings; review is a revision-bound transition context with immutable votes, not an independent approval request object.

areas.title: Manual development links and stage assignment rules
areas.summary: Current integration features are manually maintained development URLs and stage-entry assignee rules. Automatic Git provider synchronization, build webhooks and a general trigger/action automation builder are outside the implemented boundary.

areas.title: Issues, discovery, editing, bulk actions and saved searches
areas.summary: Atomic current issue behaviors; web-only composition is distinguished from shared typed services. Watch/unwatch belongs to notifications.

areas.title: MCP protocol, account connections and native Antigravity plugin
areas.summary: Business tool behavior is canonical in its domain. This area documents authentication, browser-only credential management, OAuth, activity privacy, proxy onboarding and native plugin interaction. Real managed provider/shared deployment remains pending. Related test paths are references, not proof of per-case execution.

areas.title: Watching, private inbox and notification delivery
areas.summary: Canonical owner of watch/unwatch. Event creation, preference and worker behavior are documented independently from external SMTP delivery. Related test files are references only; no tests were executed for this inventory.

areas.title: Epics, releases, issue planning and Kanban reports
areas.summary: Current planning groups work into epics/releases and reports actual Kanban completion history. Planning items are not issue hierarchy nodes or Scrum sprints; this catalog does not count roadmap or time-log capabilities as implemented.

areas.title: Shared API, authorization and transport rules
areas.summary: Cross-feature service and transport invariants. These are separately identifiable contract/operational cases, not a claim that one generic test proves every endpoint.

areas.title: Projects and project membership
areas.summary: Current project directory, lifecycle, read permissions, membership administration and eligible-person discovery. Workflow and board configuration have separate canonical areas.

areas.title: Subtasks, blockers and retained issue relations
areas.summary: Independent child work, guarded prerequisite graph, live candidate lookup and relates-to/duplicate links.

areas.title: CSV issue import and export
areas.summary: File intake, mapping, nonmutating preview, explicit confirmation, deduplicated import and bounded filtered export. Related test references do not certify per-case coverage or execution.

areas.title: Workflows, stages, transitions, policies and migration
areas.summary: Canonical owner for workflow configuration, type bindings and transition-policy configuration. Board columns map these stages but do not define workflows. Review requests and votes belong to issue collaboration.

areas.title: Workspace, navigation and shared controls
areas.summary: Current shell, workspace dashboard, global discovery, shared input behavior and foreground refresh. Domain-specific editors and permissions are documented in their own areas.

cases.title: Recheck access after storage read
preconditions: The actor is signed in with current project write access unless this case explicitly changes that access.
steps: Lose access while private bytes are being loaded.
expected: Post-I/O authorization prevents returning protected bytes.
notes: The native Playwright scenario uses the normal Download action and a Linux write lease on only its freshly uploaded, isolated local text object. The kernel's SIGIO proves the real Go storage open is waiting; actual project membership is removed before releasing the lease. The actual typed 404 response contains no protected bytes, no browser download occurs, and the UI shows the denial. The lease fixture does not modify stored bytes or metadata. Finally cleanup restores membership and verifies the original content through the service.

This verifies the real local object-store post-I/O authorization boundary without an application test hook. It does not verify Google Cloud Storage provider behavior. Additional deterministic account-revocation and upload interleavings remain supplemental Go service evidence in docs/use-cases/service-evidence.json; those do not substitute for browser surface evidence.

cases.title: Preserve mail commit uncertainty
preconditions: The actor is active and approved; issue notifications refer to currently accessible project content unless a denial case states otherwise.
steps: Allow a real local SMTP sink to acknowledge the owned DATA payload, hold only that delivery’s QUIT response, and kill only the owned secondary worker with SIGKILL before Send returns or its database transaction commits.
Observe the retained pending row, then restart the captured server and let it retry the same delivery.
expected: The acknowledged external SMTP acceptance is not rolled back with the database transaction: the retained row remains pending with attempt 0 after the crash.
The retry may be acknowledged a second time with the same stable Message-ID, then persist sent with attempt 1; this demonstrates at-least-once mail and does not promise duplicate suppression.
notes: This case documents the send-before-commit boundary, not a guarantee of duplicate suppression.
Local acceptance clarifies crash-before-commit rather than claiming a PostgreSQL COMMIT error was injected. Intended-provider receipt remains a separate pending acceptance target.
A SIGKILL can prevent Go coverage counter flushing for that child; runtime case evidence and measured source coverage must be reported separately.

The real local SMTP integration now verifies accepted DATA followed by owned-worker SIGKILL, retained pending attempt 0, and a second accepted delivery with the same Message-ID before sent attempt 1. The inherent at-least-once boundary remains documented; intended-provider acceptance remains pending separately.

cases.title: Release destroyed bulk editor ownership after a late response
preconditions: The signed-in writer has a same-tab retained native bulk draft after explicitly confirming navigation away.
The first bulk field write was accepted by the real service; its reply is held while the original bulk component has been destroyed and the clean Backlog route is active.
steps: Deliver the accepted bulk reply after the original component is destroyed.
Use the visible Issues link to leave the clean Backlog route in the same signed-in tab.
expected: The late completion does not re-register the destroyed bulk editor as active dirty work: the clean Backlog route leaves successfully without an unrelated draft confirmation.
notes: The browser fixture holds the actual accepted server reply and uses ordinary links and the native leave confirmation. No Angular internals or fabricated server responses are used.

This atomic case covers dirty-ownership release only. Same-tab draft restoration and exact accepted-item replay remain independently required by UC-SHL-0072 and UC-ISS-0165; they are not inferred from this case.
